BREAKING: Tether purchased +14 tonnes of gold in Q2 2026, bringing total holdings to a record 146 tonnes, now worth ~$18.8 billion.

This follows gold purchases of +53 tonnes between Q3 2025 and Q1 2026.

Tether’s gold holdings have more than doubled since Q1 2025, while their value has nearly tripled over the same period.

This makes the company the largest known private holder of gold outside of central banks and governments.

In the first half of 2026, only 4 central banks bought more gold than Tether: Poland, Uzbekistan, China, and Kazakhstan.

Tether is now competing with central banks for gold after the correction.

The US services sector is again signaling stagflation:

ISM Services PMI rose +0.1 point in July, to 54.1, while the employment index dropped -3.6 points, to 47.4, the lowest reading since March and back in contraction territory.

This is also the 2nd-lowest reading since October and marks the 4th monthly contraction over the last 5.

At the same time, the prices paid index surged +2.6 points, to 70.3, near the highest since October 2022.

Prices paid have now trended higher for over 2 years, rising +16.9 points since March 2024.

In other words, the economy is increasingly under pressure from both rising prices and a weakening labor market.

The threat of stagflation is intensifying.

Global passive equity fund inflows are skyrocketing:

Passive equity funds across developed and emerging markets attracted a record +$250 billion in inflows over the last 4 weeks.

Over the same timeframe, active funds recorded -$50 billion in outflows.

This brings combined 4-week flows across passive and active equity funds to +$200 billion, an all-time high.

This surpasses the previous record of +$165 billion set in early 2021, when both passive and active funds recorded inflows.

Overall, passive equity fund inflows have more than quadrupled since mid-2025.

Passive investing remains exceptionally popular.

BREAKING: US-listed ETFs have attracted +$1.2 trillion in inflows year-to-date, the largest amount at this point of the year on record.

This figure is already double the inflows recorded over the same period in 2025.

This has also surpassed every full-year total in history except 2025, which saw +$1.5 trillion in inflows.

At the current pace, US-listed ETFs are on track to exceed +$2.1 trillion in annual inflows for the first time, ~50% above last year's all-time high.

Meanwhile, the semiconductor ETFs, $SMH and $SOXX, posted a combined +$13 billion in inflows in July, the largest monthly total on record.

ETF demand is surging at an unprecedented rate.

Oil industry profits are soaring:

Earnings for 5 major Western oil companies are on track to surge to ~$44 billion in Q2 2026, the 3rd-largest quarterly total on record.

The only quarters with larger profits were Q2 and Q3 2022, when oil prices exceeded $120/barrel.

This comes as ExxonMobil, $XOM, posted $14.7 billion in profit, its strongest quarter since Q3 2022.

At the same time, Chevron, $CVX, reported a record $12.1 billion quarterly profit, surpassing its previous high set in 2022.

Meanwhile, Shell, $SHEL, reported $9.8 billion in profit in Q2, its 2nd-largest quarterly profit in the company's history.

Oil companies are cashing-in massive gains amid the Iran War.

The US manufacturing recovery is accelerating:

ISM Manufacturing PMI rose +2.3 points in July, to 55.6, the highest since May 2022.

This marks the 7th consecutive monthly expansion.

Since December 2025, the index has surged +7.7 points, the biggest increase since the 2020 pandemic recovery.

This comes as new orders rose +0.7 points, to 56.7, the 3rd-highest since February 2022, pointing to further strength ahead.

At the same time, the employment index jumped +3.1 points, to 52.8, the highest since August 2022, marking the first monthly expansion since January 2025.

Meanwhile, prices paid fell -1.9 points, to 71.1, the lowest since February, posting the 3rd consecutive monthly decline by a total of -13.5 points. 

Manufacturing activity is gaining momentum.

Chinese investors are rotating back into gold:

China's gold-backed ETFs have recorded 14 consecutive daily inflows ending Monday, the longest streak since March.

Over this period, these funds have attracted +$1.2 billion.

The largest single-day inflow during this streak totaled +$370 million.

Before this rebound, China's gold-backed ETFs recorded outflows in 38 of 44 trading sessions.

This comes as elevated volatility in China's stock market has renewed interest in alternative assets, particularly among institutional investors.

Chinese investors are increasingly bullish on gold.
